source:
@@U00219@@
What can be nicer on Sundays and holidays than to talk of war or rumors of it, while far off somewhere, maybe in Turkey, they're pounding each others’ heads together. You stand at the window, draining your glass, and watch bright ships sail downstream, and then at twilight wend your way back home and thank God for the blessings of peace.

@@U00221@@
Right you are! There I agree! Let them bust each others’ heads and turn the world all topsy-turvy, as long as we're true to our good old German customs.

@@U00223@@
(To the CITIZENS’ DAUGHTERS.)

@@U00224@@
Mercy! Aren't we all decked out! What fine young things you ladies look! Who wouldn't love to win prizes like you? Now, now, not so snooty! It’s all right, believe me, dearies, I know how to get you what you want.

@@U00226@@
Come, Agatha! I refuse to be seen in public places with these dreadful witches. All the same, last Halloween she showed me my future lover in the flesh.

@@U00228@@
She showed me mine in a crystal ball; a soldier with all his bold comrades. I look around for him everywhere, and yet I never seem to find him.
translation:
@@U00219@@
在周日和节假日，还有什么比谈论战争或有关战争的谣言更好的事情了，而在遥远的某个地方，也许是在土耳其，他们在一起互相敲打着对方的头。你站在窗前，喝干酒杯，看着明亮的船只顺流而下，然后在黄昏时分踏上回家的路，感谢上帝赐予和平的祝福。

@@U00221@@
你是对的！我同意！只要我们忠于我们古老的德国习俗，就让他们互相打架，把世界搅得天翻地覆吧。

@@U00223@@
（致公民的女儿们。）

@@U00224@@
怜悯！我们还不是都装出来了！你们女士们看上去多么年轻啊！谁不想像你一样赢得奖品？现在，现在，不要那么傲慢了！没关系，相信我，亲爱的，我知道如何让你得到你想要的。

@@U00226@@
来吧，阿加莎！我拒绝与这些可怕的女巫一起出现在公共场所。尽管如此，去年万圣节她向我展示了我未来的情人的真身。

@@U00228@@
她给我看了我的水晶球；一名士兵和他所有勇敢的战友。我到处寻找他，但似乎从来没有找到过他。
